verses.14:1: Senhor, quem habitará {tabernaculo}? * ou quem {requiescet} no vosso monte santo?
verses.14:2: {q2} {ingreditur} sem mancha, * e pratica a justiça:
verses.14:3a: {q3a} fala a verdade no seu coração, * {q3a2} {dolum}:
verses.14:4a: {adnihilum}: * mas {glorificat} os que temem o Senhor:
verses.14:4b: {q4b} jura ao seu próximo, e {decipit}, * {q4b2} não deu o seu dinheiro {usuram}, {nec} {munera} contra o inocente.

decisions.why: Glossary: tabernáculum → tenda (open, Ps 90:10), whose row says the same word must serve God's tent (14:1, 30:21, 60:5). Applied so far: 90:10 'da tua tenda', 117:15 'nas tendas dos justos'. 31 lines have the word (grep), God's and men's alike (26:5 in tabernáculo suo, 60:5 Inhabitábo in tabernáculo tuo, 83:2 Quam dilécta tabernácula tua; 83:11 tabernáculis peccatórum, 77:51 tabernáculis Cham). The Greek σκήνωμα, a tent-dwelling. Douay-Rheims 'tabernacle'; Matos Soares 1932 'tabernáculo'; the Diurnal 'Sob a tua tenda'.

options.label: na vossa tenda
options.note: Ruling: the glossary's word, the concrete tent (rule 5), one word for God's and men's dwellings as the Latin has; the Diurnal's word too. 'Tabernáculo' in Brazil is first the tabernacle of a church, which would read the Mass into the psalm.

options.label: no vosso tabernáculo
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 and Douay-Rheims: the traditional word, heard today as the church tabernacle; and it cannot serve 77:51 or 83:11 (the tents of Cham, of sinners).

decisions.latin: aut quis requiéscet in monte sancto tuo
decisions.why: requiéscere: 4:9 'dormirei e repousarei' (Ps 4), 15:9 caro mea requiéscet in spe (the glossary row ínsuper et already writes 'repousará na esperança'), 54:7 volábo, et requiéscam (grep: four lines). The Greek here is κατασκηνώσει ('will encamp, dwell') — the Latin reads 'rest'. monte sancto → 'monte santo', adjective after, as 2:6 'o seu monte santo' (3:5, 42:3, 47:2, 98:9 have the same phrase). Douay-Rheims 'rest in thy holy hill'; Matos Soares 1932 'descansará no teu santo monte'.

options.label: repousará
options.note: Ruling: one verb for requiéscere in all four places, as 4:9 has it; 15:9 follows in the next psalm.

options.label: descansará
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: plainer; 4:9 has 'repousarei', so the echo would be lost.

decisions.latin: Qui … qui … Qui … qui … Qui (the answer to 'quis')
decisions.why: The psalm answers 'quis?' with six relative clauses (Qui ingréditur, Qui lóquitur, qui non egit, Qui jurat, qui pecúniam, Qui facit); the Greek has participles. The repetition is the psalm's shape and is kept at the head of each verse. Douay-Rheims 'He that … who …'; Matos Soares 1932 'O que … o que …'; the Diurnal 'Aquele que'.

options.label: Aquele que … que
options.note: Ruling: 'Aquele que' at the head of each verse, where the Latin has a capital Qui; the second 'qui' of 14:3a and 14:4b, which continues the same man, as bare 'que'. 'O que' at the head of a verse can be heard as 'what' ('O que anda sem mancha …?'); 'Aquele que' cannot. The Diurnal's form.

options.label: O que … o que
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: shorter, every 'qui' the same; 'O que' can be taken for 'what'.

options.label: Quem … quem
options.note: Echoes the question's 'quem' of 14:1; but a bare 'Quem' at the head of 14:2 is heard as a new question.

decisions.why: ingrédi is 'to enter' and also 'to go, walk, proceed' (Lewis & Short, 'to go into, to enter … to enter upon'); the Greek is πορευόμενος, 'walking, going'. The glossary gives 'entrar' to íngredi / intráre in 117:19 (the gates), and 'andar' to ambuláre and to abíre (1:1) because the Greek there is πορεύομαι. The same sense comes back in 25:1, 25:11 ego in innocéntia mea ingréssus sum (grep). sine mácula → 'sem mancha' (the glossary's option for immaculátus, 118:1 'imaculados' — here the Latin has the phrase). Douay-Rheims 'walketh without blemish'; Matos Soares 1932 'vive na inocência' (explains); the Diurnal 'caminha na inocência'.

options.label: anda
options.note: Ruling: the walking sense the Greek fixes (πορευόμενος), and the glossary's verb for πορεύομαι (ambuláre, abíre); 25:1 and 25:11 can follow ('andei na minha inocência').

options.label: caminha
options.note: The Diurnal's verb; a word of its own for ingrédi, but 'caminhar' is kept away from via → caminho.

options.label: entra
options.note: The verb's first sense, and a resonance with the tent of 14:1 (who enters it); but the Greek and Douay-Rheims read 'walks', and 'entra sem mancha' says an act where the Latin describes a life.

decisions.latin: qui non egit dolum in lingua sua
decisions.why: Glossary: dolus → engano (open, Ps 5). The Greek is one verb (ὃς οὐκ ἐδόλωσεν), as at 5:11a / 13:3b linguis suis dolóse agébant → 'com as suas línguas enganavam'. But this psalm has décipere too (14:4b et non décipit), a different Latin verb and a different Greek (ἀθετῶν, 'setting aside, breaking faith'), which wants 'enganar' more than dolus does. 23:4 nec jurávit in dolo próximo suo is this psalm's cousin. Douay-Rheims 'who hath not used deceit in his tongue'; Matos Soares 1932 'não forjou enganos com a sua língua'. Heard (draft 1): the stylist — «A combinação de “usou de” com “na sua língua” soa montada sobre o latim e dificulta a compreensão ao ouvir» → ‘que não praticou engano com a sua língua’. The Latinist passed draft 1.

options.label: não usou de engano com a sua língua

forms.dolum: não usou de engano com a sua língua

options.note: Ruling (draft 2): the stylist’s preposition taken — ‘in lingua sua’ is instrumental, as linguis suis in 13:3b / 5:11a (‘com as suas línguas’); a preposition follows Portuguese use (D2). His verb ‘praticou’ refused: ‘praticar’ is operári’s, and operátur justítiam stands in the verse before (‘pratica a justiça’) — egit and operátur would become one verb. dolus keeps its noun; ‘enganar’ stays free for décipere (14:4b).

options.label: não usou de engano na sua língua

forms.dolum: não usou de engano na sua língua

options.note: Draft 1. dolus keeps its noun ('engano', the glossary's), the light verb yields to 'usar de' (Douay-Rheims' 'used deceit'), 'in lingua' kept as 'na sua língua'. It leaves the verb 'enganar' to décipere in 14:4b, so two Latin words stay two in one psalm (a noun and a verb of one Portuguese family, the least that can be done).

options.label: não enganou com a sua língua

forms.dolum: não enganou com a sua língua

options.note: The Greek's one verb, as 5:11a / 13:3b 'com as suas línguas enganavam' (the echo of the Latin's lingua + dolus); but then 14:4b's décipere is the same verb.

options.label: não forjou engano com a sua língua

forms.dolum: não forjou engano com a sua língua

options.note: Matos Soares 1932's verb: an image the Latin (agere) does not have.

options.label: não praticou engano com a sua língua

forms.dolum: não praticou engano com a sua língua

options.note: The stylist’s line. Refused: ‘praticar’ is operári’s (14:2 ‘pratica a justiça’, one verse before).

decisions.why: próximus → próximo (glossary), a proparoxytone, which the glossary says needs a word after it at a cadence (11:3). The Latin ends the colon on 'malum'. Douay-Rheims 'Nor hath done evil to his neighbour'; Matos Soares 1932 'nem fez mal ao seu semelhante'. Heard (draft 1): the stylist — «A separação de “fez” e “mal” retarda uma expressão naturalmente imediata na fala» → ‘nem fez mal ao seu próximo’. Refused: it puts the proparoxytone ‘próximo’ at the mediant (rule 4; the glossary row próximus, and Ps 11:3 was recast for the same reason); his line is option 2.

options.label: fez ao seu próximo o mal

forms.proximo: fez ao seu próximo o mal

options.note: Ruling: the Latin's order (dative before the object), the mediant on the stressed 'mal' as the Latin's is on 'malum'.

options.label: fez mal ao seu próximo
options.note: The stylist’s line (the everyday order); the mediant falls on the proparoxytone ‘próximo’ (rule 4).

decisions.latin: et oppróbrium non accépit advérsus próximos suos
decisions.why: 'Nor took up a reproach against his neighbours' — he did not receive, lend himself to, a slander on them (ὀνειδισμὸν οὐκ ἔλαβεν ἐπὶ τοὺς ἔγγιστα αὐτοῦ). oppróbrium → afronta (glossary, open; 'opróbrio' failed two blind readers in Ps 118). accípere is said again in 14:4b (múnera … non accépit) and is kept one verb, 'aceitar'. próximos (the Greek has another word here, ἔγγιστα, 'those nearest'; the Latin repeats próximus) → 'próximos', which must not end the verse (proparoxytone). Douay-Rheims 'nor taken up a reproach against his neighbours'; Matos Soares 1932 'nem consentiu que fossem infamados os seus próximos' (explains).

options.label: e contra os seus próximos não aceitou afronta

forms.opprobrium: e contra os seus próximos não aceitou afronta

options.note: Ruling: every word kept; the adverbial phrase first so that the verse ends on 'afronta' (paroxytone), not on 'próximos'. 'Aceitar' as in 14:4b (accépit twice). To be tested on the blind reader: 'não aceitou afronta' may be heard as 'did not put up with an insult'.

options.label: e não aceitou afronta contra os seus próximos

forms.opprobrium: e não aceitou afronta contra os seus próximos

options.note: The Latin's order; ends on the proparoxytone 'próximos'.

options.label: e não acolheu afronta contra os seus próximos

forms.opprobrium: e não acolheu afronta contra os seus próximos

options.note: 'Acolher' says 'took up, gave room to' more clearly, but loses the echo with 14:4b's accépit and is the verb proposed for suscípere.

decisions.latin: Ad níhilum dedúctus est in conspéctu ejus malígnus
decisions.why: dedúcere ad níhilum: 'bring to nothing' (Greek ἐξουδένωται, 'is set at nought'). The same phrase with dedúcere is 58:9, 59:14 = 107:14 (ad níhilum dedúcet), and with redígere 72:20, 77:59, 72:21 ad níhilum redáctus sum (grep; the Greek of those not checked). D22/D25: dedúcere is 'guiar' for guidance, 'fazer descer ao pó' for 7:6 — neither fits. malígnus → malvado (settled, D24). in conspéctu ejus → 'à vista dele' (the open proposal, 5:9; 9:26a 'Não há Deus à vista dele'); 'ejus' is open between the just man and God, as 'dele' is. Douay-Rheims 'In his sight the malignant is brought to nothing'; Matos Soares 1932 'Na sua apreciação considera o malvado como um nada' (explains). Heard (draft 1): the stylist — «“À vista dele” soa como indicação de algo presenciado fisicamente; “aos olhos dele” exprime com mais naturalidade esse olhar que julga». The blind reader heard ‘À vista dele’ first as ‘aos olhos do homem descrito’ — the judging look, rightly.

options.label: À vista dele, o malvado foi reduzido a nada

forms.adnihilum: À vista dele, o malvado foi reduzido a nada

options.note: Ruling: 'reduzir' is re-dúcere, the Latin's own verb with another prefix, and 'reduzido a nada' is the living idiom; the passive perfect kept; natural order, the colon ending on the paroxytone 'nada'. 58:9, 59:14, 107:14 (dedúcet) can say 'reduzirá a nada', and 72:21 redáctus sum 'fui reduzido a nada' — if the Greek there differs, those verses decide.

options.label: Aos olhos dele, o malvado foi reduzido a nada

forms.adnihilum: Aos olhos dele, o malvado foi reduzido a nada

options.note: The stylist’s line. Refused: ‘olho’ is óculus’s word (ante óculos → diante dos olhos, 13:3d) and conspéctus keeps ‘vista’ (glossary, open; 9:20, 9:26a); the blind reader heard ‘à vista dele’ as the judging look, so nothing is lost by it.

options.label: Foi reduzido a nada à sua vista o malvado

forms.adnihilum: Foi reduzido a nada à sua vista o malvado

options.note: The Latin's order, 'ad níhilum' first; heavy.

options.label: Na sua apreciação considera o malvado como um nada

forms.adnihilum: Na sua apreciação considera o malvado como um nada

options.note: Matos Soares 1932: turns the passive into the just man's judgment — an explanation.

decisions.why: glorificáre → glorificar (glossary, working; Ps 90:15, of God glorifying man). Here a man glorifies those who fear the Lord (δοξάζει). The subject is unexpressed, as in the Latin. Douay-Rheims 'he glorifieth them that fear the Lord'; Matos Soares 1932 and the Diurnal 'honra'.

options.label: glorifica
options.note: Ruling: the glossary's verb; the Latin puts God's verb (90:15 glorificábo eum) in the just man's mouth, and that is kept.

options.label: honra
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 and the Diurnal: the natural word of a man, but it is honoráre's, and the Latin's height is lowered.

decisions.latin: Qui jurat próximo suo, et non décipit
decisions.why: décipere: 'to deceive, cheat' (3 lines: 14:4b, 61:10 ut decípiant, 76:3 non sum decéptus — grep); the Greek καὶ οὐκ ἀθετῶν, 'and does not set it aside, break faith'. No object in the Latin. 23:4 nec jurávit in dolo próximo suo is the cousin line. Douay-Rheims 'and deceiveth not'; Matos Soares 1932 'e não o engana'.

options.label: não engana
options.note: Ruling: the plain verb for décipere, with no object as in the Latin; 'engano' (dolus) in 14:3a is its noun, so the two Latin words are a noun and a verb of one family.

options.label: não o engana
options.note: Matos Soares 1932: the neighbour supplied as object.

options.label: não o ilude
options.note: A verb of its own, apart from dolus; weaker.

decisions.latin: qui pecúniam suam non dedit ad usúram
decisions.why: usúra: interest on a loan (ἐπὶ τόκῳ); 54:12 usúra, et dolus, 71:14 Ex usúris et iniquitáte (grep). Douay-Rheims 'hath not put out his money to usury'; Matos Soares 1932 'não empresta o seu dinheiro com usura'.

options.label: à usura
options.note: Ruling: the cognate, which serves 54:12 and 71:14 too, where the Latin pairs it with fraud and iniquity; 'dar dinheiro à usura' is a Portuguese phrase; the verb stays 'dar' (dedit).

options.label: a juros
options.note: The everyday phrase ('dar dinheiro a juros'): what usúra meant in Latin, but it takes the reproach out of the word, which 54:12 and 71:14 need.

options.label: com usura
options.note: Matos Soares 1932's preposition (he has 'empresta').

decisions.latin: et múnera super innocéntem non accépit
decisions.why: múnera: gifts, here a bribe (δῶρα ἐπ᾿ ἀθῴοις). Elsewhere the gifts the kings bring (67:30, 71:10, 75:12 — grep), so the word must not be 'subornos'. super → 'contra' (Douay-Rheims 'against'). Matos Soares 1932 'dádivas'.

options.label: dádivas
options.note: Ruling: Matos Soares 1932's word; it serves 67:30, 71:10 and 75:12 (the kings' gifts) as well; the sense of a bribe is carried by 'contra o inocente'.

options.label: presentes
options.note: Plainer; also serves the kings.

options.label: subornos
options.note: Douay-Rheims' 'bribes': explains, and cannot serve 67:30, 71:10.

decisions.why: in ætérnum → para sempre (settled, D23); movéri → ser abalado (open; 9:27 'Não serei abalado'). The negation is the risk D27 found for 'até o fim': 'não será abalado para sempre' can be heard as 'not shaken for good' (shaken, but not for ever). D23 kept 118:93 'Para sempre não esquecerei' with the adverb first for this reason. 124:1 non commovébitur in ætérnum and 111:6 in ætérnum non commovébitur are the same thought (grep). Douay-Rheims 'shall not be moved for ever'; Matos Soares 1932 'não será jamais comovido'; the Diurnal 'jamais será abalado'. Heard (draft 1): the stylist named it the worst line of the psalm — «A anteposição de “para sempre” à negação soa estrangeira e enfraquece a segurança da conclusão» → ‘jamais será abalado’. The blind reader heard ‘Permanecerá firme’ — the right sense, with no hint of ‘not permanently’. The Latinist passed it.

options.label: para sempre não será abalado
options.note: Ruling (drafts 1–2), held against the stylist: his ‘jamais’ drops in ætérnum’s own phrase, which D23 fixed as ‘para sempre’ for all its places, and the adverb must stand before the negation, as 118:93 ‘Para sempre não esquecerei’, or the line is heard as ‘not shaken for good’ (D27’s fault at 9:19). Heard rightly by the blind reader. For Gustavo’s ear: this is the place where D23 costs most, and ‘jamais será abalado’ (the Diurnal, and the stylist) is one touch away. 124:1 non commovébitur in ætérnum and 111:6 will meet the same choice.

options.label: não será abalado para sempre
options.note: The Latin's order; heard as 'not shaken permanently' — the fault of 9:19b's 'até o fim'.

options.label: jamais será abalado
options.note: The stylist’s line, and the Diurnal’s (Matos Soares 1932 ‘não será jamais comovido’): the natural Portuguese for ‘never’; it drops in ætérnum’s word (D23).

decisions.latin: et múnera super innocéntem non accépit
decisions.why: The second colon of 14:4b is the psalm’s longest (27 Latin syllables). The stylist: «A vírgula seguida de “e não” provoca uma retomada pesada» → ‘nem aceitou dádivas’. ‘nem’ is ‘e não’ in one word — grammar (D2).

options.label: nem aceitou
options.note: Ruling (draft 2): the stylist’s conjunction; every word of the Latin kept, accépit still ‘aceitou’ as in 14:3b. His dropping of the article (‘seu dinheiro’) not taken: the glossary keeps the article before possessives.

options.label: e não aceitou
options.note: Draft 1: ‘et … non’ word for word.

choices.14:1: The psalm begins at 14:1 (the titulus Psalmus David is out, D7). Two questions, each 'quem' as the Latin's 'quis'. Ps 23:3 (Quis ascéndet in montem Dómini? aut quis stabit in loco sancto ejus?) is the cousin of this verse, not a twin.
choices.14:2: operári justítiam → 'praticar a justiça' (glossary: operári → praticar; the row fácere judícium names 14:2).
choices.14:3a: loqui veritátem → ‘falar a verdade’ (véritas → verdade, glossary); in corde suo → ‘no seu coração’, as the Latin. in lingua sua → ‘com a sua língua’: the instrumental in, as linguis suis in 13:3b.
choices.14:3b: Nec → 'nem', continuing the list of 14:3a. The Greek has two words for 'neighbour' (πλησίον, then ἔγγιστα); the Latin has próximus twice and so does the Portuguese.
choices.14:4b: The inline '(5a)' of DO is not reproduced (rule 4). próximus → 'próximo' (not at a cadence here). accépit → 'aceitou', the same verb as 14:3b. innocens → 'inocente' (innocéntia → inocência, glossary). The second colon is long (the Latin's is 27 syllables).
choices.14:5b: Qui facit hæc → 'Aquele que faz estas coisas' (hæc, neuter plural).

audit.note: Latin = DO Psalm14.txt, seven prayed verses with DO's ids (14:1, 2, 3a, 3b, 4a, 4b, 5b; 14:4b carries the inline '(5a)'). Collated against the Clementine Vulgate fetched from Bolls (consult/bolls-VULG-19-14.json): identical.

Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps014.md. Sense from the Vulgate family (Douay-Rheims; Matos Soares 1932 by its text layer, his glosses ignored). The Diurnal has the psalm, from the Hebrew: diction only; refused where it follows the Hebrew (14:4a 'O que despreza com o olhar o infame', 14:4b 'não trai o juramento que o prejudica'). DO's Portuguese not used (D12). Lewis & Short read for ingredior. Repeats found with ps005/grep_latin.py: tabernáculum (31 lines), monte sancto (6), requiéscere (4), jurare (10; 23:4 nec jurávit in dolo próximo suo is the cousin), décipere (3), usúra (3 + 40:8 false hit), múnera (4), innocens (16), ad níhilum (8), commovéri (13; 124:1 non commovébitur in ætérnum). Septuagintal readings kept where the Latin has them against the Hebrew: 14:4a 'foi reduzido a nada … o malvado' (not the Hebrew's 'the reprobate is despised in his eyes'), 14:4b 'e não engana' (not 'swears to his own hurt'). Glossary applied: tenda, praticar a justiça, engano, malvado (D24), à vista de, glorificar, para sempre (D23), ser abalado. Decisions: 13.

Draft 1: hard pass. Soft flags accepted: 14:1 first colon −4 (‘na vossa tenda’ for ‘in tabernáculo tuo’ — the shorter word is the point); 14:4b first colon +4 (‘Aquele que’ and the article); 14:5b first colon +5 (‘Aquele que faz estas coisas’ for ‘Qui facit hæc’: the psalm’s ‘Qui’ is ‘Aquele que’ throughout, and hæc, a neuter plural, needs a noun). No rhyme flag.

Draft 1. Clean: no remark on any verse; the marks confirmed. Passed in particular ‘na vossa tenda’, ‘Aquele que anda sem mancha’, ‘não usou de engano na sua língua’, ‘e contra os seus próximos não aceitou afronta’, ‘À vista dele, o malvado foi reduzido a nada’, ‘glorifica’, ‘à usura’, ‘dádivas’, ‘para sempre não será abalado’.

Draft 1. Five verses; best 14:2, worst 14:5b. «O salmo tem sobriedade, imagens concretas e cadências regulares … Algumas construções ainda deixam ouvir a tradução, sobretudo na conclusão.» Two taken (one in part), three refused with options.

outcomes.remark: ‘usou de … na sua língua’ sounds built on the Latin → ‘que não praticou engano com a sua língua’
outcomes.reason: The preposition taken (‘com a sua língua’, the instrumental in, as 13:3b). His verb refused and kept as an option: ‘praticar’ is operári’s, and 14:2 has ‘pratica a justiça’ one verse before.

outcomes.remark: ‘fez ao seu próximo o mal’ separates ‘fez’ and ‘mal’ → ‘nem fez mal ao seu próximo’
outcomes.reason: Rule 4: it puts the proparoxytone ‘próximo’ at the mediant (as Ps 11:3 was recast to avoid).

outcomes.remark: ‘À vista dele’ sounds like physical presence → ‘Aos olhos dele’
outcomes.reason: ‘olho’ is óculus’s; conspéctus keeps ‘vista’ (glossary; 9:20, 9:26a); the blind reader heard the judging look rightly.

outcomes.remark: ‘, e não aceitou’ is a heavy restart in a long colon → ‘nem aceitou’
outcomes.reason: ‘nem’ is ‘e não’ — grammar (D2). His dropped article (‘seu dinheiro’) not taken.

outcomes.remark: ‘para sempre’ before the negation sounds foreign and weakens the close → ‘jamais será abalado’ (worst line)
outcomes.reason: D23 (in ætérnum → para sempre) and the 118:93 build, which is what keeps ‘never’ from being heard as ‘not for good’; the blind reader heard ‘Permanecerá firme’. For Gustavo’s ear.

audit.note: Draft 1, Portuguese only. 16 items, 1 unknown word (usura). No wrong first hearing. Tests passed: ‘e contra os seus próximos não aceitou afronta’ heard as ‘did not tolerate offences against his neighbours’ (the second hearing, ‘did not take up an accusation against them’, is the Latin’s exactly; the first is near it); ‘para sempre não será abalado’ heard as ‘permanecerá firme’ — no ‘not permanently’; ‘À vista dele’ heard as the just man’s judging look.

outcomes.remark: ‘habitará na vossa tenda’: a real tent / living with the Lord (heard first)
outcomes.reason: The Latin’s image, both.

outcomes.remark: ‘repousará no vosso monte santo’: a sacred mountain / peace with the Lord
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly.

outcomes.remark: ‘anda sem mancha’: blameless life (heard first) / clean clothes
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly.

outcomes.remark: ‘pratica a justiça’: acts justly (heard first) / applies the law
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly.

outcomes.remark: ‘fala a verdade no seu coração’: sincere (heard first) / speaks truth only inwardly
outcomes.reason: in corde suo is as open.

outcomes.remark: ‘próximo / próximos’: others in general / people close to him (plural)
outcomes.reason: The Latin’s one word, singular and plural.

outcomes.remark: ‘não aceitou afronta’: did not tolerate offences against them (heard first) / did not take up an accusation against them
outcomes.reason: Both are inside ‘oppróbrium non accépit advérsus’; the second is the Latin’s letter, the first its effect.

outcomes.remark: ‘À vista dele’: the just man (heard first) / the Lord
outcomes.reason: ejus is as open.

outcomes.remark: ‘reduzido a nada’: esteemed worthless / destroyed before him (heard first)
outcomes.reason: ad níhilum dedúctus est holds both (the Greek leans to the first); Douay-Rheims is as open.

outcomes.remark: ‘glorifica’: the just man (heard first) / the Lord / the malvado
outcomes.reason: The Latin leaves the subject unexpressed the same way; ‘mas’ (autem) sets it against the malvado.

outcomes.remark: ‘temem o Senhor’: reverence (heard first) / fear
outcomes.reason: timére holds both.

outcomes.remark: ‘jura ao seu próximo’: a promise (heard first) / an oath of fact
outcomes.reason: Heard rightly.

outcomes.remark: ‘à usura’: excessive interest (heard first) / any interest
outcomes.reason: usúra is interest; the reproach the Portuguese word carries is the psalter’s own (54:12, 71:14).

outcomes.remark: ‘dádivas contra o inocente’: a bribe to harm him (heard first)
outcomes.reason: Heard as meant, without the word ‘suborno’.

outcomes.remark: ‘estas coisas’: all the conduct named (heard first) / only the last verse’s
outcomes.reason: hæc is as open.

outcomes.remark: ‘não será abalado’: firm (heard first) / spared every setback
outcomes.reason: movéri holds both.

outcomes.remark: unknown word: usura
outcomes.reason: The cognate, needed for 54:12 and 71:14; heard rightly by the reader who knows it; ‘a juros’ is option 2.
